four_player_fight.model: tools/tests/test_scarlet_levels.py dense_mix: Graceful Ordeal bars 19-23 at the owner's sliders under the local organ and three other players' scythe, quill and censers at their real rates, sound budgets and voice limits; each Raid warning laid over it at ten places; the measure is the best 1/3-octave band against everything else in the warning's loudest 400 ms (median of ten). With the crescent cues the other player's scythe also sheds a volley once per 100-tick measure and rings a break at +39, +57, +75, +93, +122, +128, +134, +140 and +146 ticks: nine breaks, one per crescent a held loop throws (four singles 30 ticks after their throws, the volley's five one by one 6 ticks apart, the closest a break rings, 30 ticks after it is shed), the most a held loop rings (the 8-crescent cap bounds how many fly at once, not how many break, and the 6-tick throttle would allow sixteen). The same nine spread evenly (+39, +50, +61, +72, +83, +95, +106, +117, +128) are a second layout, bounded but not pinned by the test
four_player_fight.correction: An earlier draft of this change modelled six breaks (the volley's five ringing once or twice) and called that the most a held loop allows, which it is not: a swarm breaks the volley's five one by one. The nine-break model replaces it (smallest margin 3.54 to 3.42 dB, largest loss 0.09 to 0.2 dB in the densest layout, 0.23 dB spread evenly); the files, offsets and every other relation are unchanged
four_player_fight.result: every warning keeps at least 3.42 dB in every scenario and layout (the floor is 3.0) and at least 0.3.80's margin, and loses at most 0.23 dB against the shipped build without the crescent cues (bound 0.25); the existing test's model (without the crescent cues) is unchanged and its numbers hold
